stem: What gap did μSAM's authors identify in earlier studies applying SAM to medical imaging, histopathology and neuroimaging?
choices: They retrained SAM but dropped its interactive segmentation
They used only the default SAM without retraining for their domain
They applied SAM only to volumetric rather than 2D data
They replaced SAM's image encoder with a convolutional network
answer: They used only the default SAM without retraining for their domain
label: Intro · prior work

stem: What shortcoming of default SAM on microscopy cell images motivated μSAM's fine-tuning?
choices: It splits single cells into several fragments
It fails to segment cells at image borders
It segments clusters of cells as a single object
It ignores negative point annotations entirely
answer: It segments clusters of cells as a single object
label: Results · default SAM failure

stem: What does the additional decoder that μSAM adds to SAM for automatic instance segmentation (AIS) predict?
choices: A grid of point prompts filtered for overlapping masks
Bounding boxes plus a per-object confidence score
Foreground plus affinities between neighbouring pixels
Foreground plus distances to object centers and boundaries
answer: Foreground plus distances to object centers and boundaries
label: Results · AIS decoder

stem: In μSAM's simulated interactive evaluation, how many correction iterations, each adding a positive and a negative point from prediction errors, follow the initial prompt?
choices: Seven
Three
Five
Ten
answer: Seven
label: Results · interactive evaluation

stem: Which SAM image-encoder size did the μSAM authors find gave the best trade-off between runtime and quality for the LIVECell experiments?
choices: ViT-T (tiny)
ViT-L (large)
ViT-B (base)
ViT-H (huge)
answer: ViT-L (large)
label: Results · encoder size

stem: On LIVECell, how did interactive segmentation with the default SAM compare with CellPose's automatic segmentation?
choices: It matched CellPose from a single box prompt
It never reached CellPose at any iteration
It matched CellPose only after several correction iterations
It exceeded CellPose from a single point prompt
answer: It matched CellPose only after several correction iterations
label: Results · LIVECell default vs CellPose

stem: On LIVECell, how did adding more corrective point annotations affect the default SAM versus the fine-tuned specialist?
choices: Only the default model improved consistently with more annotations
Both improved consistently at about the same rate
Neither improved after the first correction iteration
Only the specialist improved consistently with more annotations
answer: Only the specialist improved consistently with more annotations
label: Results · more annotations

stem: On LIVECell, how did μSAM's automatic instance segmentation (AIS) compare with a CellPose model trained on LIVECell?
choices: On par with CellPose
Clearly worse than CellPose
Clearly better than CellPose
On par only after point corrections
answer: On par with CellPose
label: Results · AIS vs CellPose (LIVECell)

stem: When μSAM fine-tuned only parts of SAM on LIVECell, which single part had the biggest impact on segmentation quality?
choices: The mask decoder
The image encoder
The prompt encoder
The new AIS decoder
answer: The image encoder
label: Results · partial fine-tuning

stem: In μSAM's LIVECell data-fraction experiment, roughly what share of the training set already gave the majority of the fine-tuning improvement?
choices: About 20–25%
About 50%
About 2–5%
About 75–80%
answer: About 2–5%
label: Results · training data fraction

stem: Why did μSAM train separate generalist models for light and electron microscopy rather than one model?
choices: Combined LM and EM training data exceeded available GPU memory
EM images cannot be converted to SAM's RGB input format
Licensing of the EM datasets forbade mixing with LM data
A single model improving across modalities is not feasible with SAM's architecture
answer: A single model improving across modalities is not feasible with SAM's architecture
label: Results · separate generalists

stem: How did μSAM's LM generalist compare with the single-dataset specialist models on their datasets?
choices: Similar or better, except AIS on LIVECell
Similar or better, except AIS on TissueNet
Consistently worse, except on LIVECell
Similar or better, except interactive on DeepBacs
answer: Similar or better, except AIS on LIVECell
label: Results · generalist vs specialist

stem: On which LM training dataset did the generalist's automatic segmentation (AIS) fall short of CellPose?
choices: LIVECell
TissueNet
DeepBacs
NeurIPS CellSeg
answer: TissueNet
label: Results · TissueNet exception

stem: What reason did μSAM's authors give for the generalist's weaker automatic segmentation on TissueNet?
choices: Its cells are too small for SAM's patch size
It is histopathology, a modality absent from training
Its two channels do not map well to SAM's RGB input
Its annotations mark nuclei rather than whole cells
answer: Its two channels do not map well to SAM's RGB input
label: Results · TissueNet reason

stem: Why did μSAM's authors call their comparison against CellPose cyto2 on DeepBacs, PlantSeg (Root) and NeurIPS CellSeg biased in their favour?
choices: cyto2 was run without its recommended diameter setting
Those datasets were scored only with interactive prompts
μSAM was evaluated at a looser IoU threshold there
μSAM was trained on those datasets' training splits and cyto2 was not
answer: μSAM was trained on those datasets' training splits and cyto2 was not
label: Results · biased comparison

stem: Which of these datasets served as an out-of-domain test for μSAM's LM generalist (image setting not represented in training)?
choices: COVID IF
TissueNet
DeepBacs
LIVECell
answer: COVID IF
label: Results · out-of-domain LM data

stem: Why was the Mouse Embryo dataset a particularly difficult test for μSAM's LM generalist?
choices: It is a different imaging modality
Its cells are small
It has two input channels
Its cells are densely overlapping in 3D
answer: Its cells are small
label: Results · Mouse Embryo

stem: On Lizard (histopathology) and Mouse Embryo, where no automated method worked well, what did give good results?
choices: Automatic AIS with the generalist, though not AMG
CellPose cyto2 automatic segmentation, though not μSAM
Interactive segmentation, improved further by the generalist
AMG with the default SAM, though not AIS
answer: Interactive segmentation, improved further by the generalist
label: Results · hard out-of-domain sets

stem: How do μSAM's authors characterise their LM generalist's automatic segmentation relative to CellPose?
choices: Better quality in most settings, but no interactive mode
Lower quality, offset by much faster inference
Better quality only on out-of-domain datasets
Similar quality for most settings, plus interactive segmentation
answer: Similar quality for most settings, plus interactive segmentation
label: Results · positioning vs CellPose

stem: Why is training a generalist segmentation model harder for electron microscopy than for light microscopy, according to μSAM?
choices: EM labels membrane-bound structures unspecifically, with no specific stain
EM images have far lower resolution than light microscopy
Public EM datasets annotate only cell outlines
EM volumes cannot be processed slice by slice
answer: EM labels membrane-bound structures unspecifically, with no specific stain
label: Results · EM difficulty

stem: For which structures does μSAM's EM generalist reliably improve segmentation?
choices: Mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum and neurites
Mitochondria, nuclei and other roundish organelles
Nuclei, cell membranes and synapses
Any membrane-bound cellular compartment
answer: Mitochondria, nuclei and other roundish organelles
label: Results · EM generalist scope

stem: Which non-EM imaging modality did μSAM include in its EM generalist evaluation, via the NucMM (Mouse) dataset?
choices: Cryo-electron tomography
Serial two-photon tomography
High-energy X-ray
Expansion light-sheet microscopy
answer: High-energy X-ray
label: Results · NucMM modality

stem: How did MitoNet compare with μSAM's AIS and AMG for automatic mitochondrion segmentation in EM?
choices: Clearly better on every dataset
Clearly worse on every dataset
Better on TEM, worse on FIBSEM
Overall comparable, varying across datasets
answer: Overall comparable, varying across datasets
label: Results · MitoNet

stem: Why is the advantage of AIS over AMG less clear in EM than in LM, according to μSAM?
choices: AMG works better on well-separated objects like mitochondria
AIS was not trained on any EM data
EM images lack the contrast AIS distance maps need
AMG was given more grid points for EM images
answer: AMG works better on well-separated objects like mitochondria
label: Results · AIS vs AMG in EM

stem: Even where AMG segments EM mitochondria about as well as AIS, why do μSAM's authors still prefer AIS in most cases?
choices: It needs no image embeddings
Its runtime is lower
It handles touching objects better
It needs no fine-tuning
answer: Its runtime is lower
label: Results · AIS preference

stem: How did μSAM's EM generalist perform on cilia and microvilli compared with default SAM?
choices: Marginally better or worse than default SAM
Worse, so specialists were required
Overall better than default SAM
Better only after LoRA fine-tuning
answer: Overall better than default SAM
label: Results · cilia and microvilli

stem: For which EM structures did μSAM's EM generalist provide only marginal benefits or even hurt segmentation?
choices: Cilia and microvilli
Mitochondria in FIBSEM volumes
Nuclei in high-energy X-ray
Endoplasmic reticulum and neurites
answer: Endoplasmic reticulum and neurites
label: Results · ER and neurites

stem: Where μSAM's EM generalist failed to help (ER and neurites), what clearly improved segmentation?
choices: Training specialist models for each task
Switching to the ViT-H encoder
Using AMG instead of AIS
Adding more point prompts per object
answer: Training specialist models for each task
label: Results · ER/neurite specialists

stem: With image embeddings precomputed, roughly how long does μSAM's interactive point or box segmentation take per object on a CPU?
choices: About 3 ms
About 30 ms
About 300 ms
About 3 s
answer: About 30 ms
label: Results · CPU interactive latency

stem: In μSAM's runtime comparison, how did AIS compare with SAM's automatic mask generation (AMG)?
choices: AMG was much faster than AIS
They ran at about the same speed
AIS was much faster than AMG
AIS was faster only on the GPU
answer: AIS was much faster than AMG
label: Results · AIS vs AMG runtime

stem: According to μSAM's runtime study, where does a GPU help most?
choices: Point-prompt mask decoding
Box-prompt mask decoding
Loading images into napari
Computing image embeddings
answer: Computing image embeddings
label: Results · GPU advantage

stem: What did μSAM find about using the ViT-H (huge) encoder instead of ViT-B or ViT-L?
choices: No better results, at higher computational cost
Better results, at higher computational cost
No better results, at similar computational cost
Better results only for EM data
answer: No better results, at higher computational cost
label: Results · ViT-H

stem: What did μSAM find about the ViT-T (tiny) encoder?
choices: Much faster, with only a small quality penalty overall
Much faster, good on simple tasks, severely degraded on others
Slower than ViT-B, but better on small objects
Much faster, but unusable for interactive prompts
answer: Much faster, good on simple tasks, severely degraded on others
label: Results · ViT-T

stem: On μSAM's benchmark hardware, roughly how long did CellPose take to segment one image?
choices: About 1.2 s on GPU and 7.5 s on CPU
About 30 ms on GPU and 0.3 s on CPU
About 0.3 s on GPU and 1.5 s on CPU
About 3 s on GPU and 15 s on CPU
answer: About 0.3 s on GPU and 1.5 s on CPU
label: Results · CellPose runtime

stem: Roughly how long does μSAM's automatic segmentation (embedding computation plus AIS) take per image on a CPU, depending on model size?
label: Results · μSAM runtime

stem: What did μSAM's resource-constrained experiment on COVID IF show about fine-tuning on 1–10 images on a CPU?
choices: It is feasible and clearly improves the model
It is feasible but gives no clear improvement
It overfits unless LoRA is used
It needs at least a GPU with 16 GB to converge
answer: It is feasible and clearly improves the model
label: Results · CPU fine-tuning

stem: How did parameter-efficient LoRA training affect μSAM's fine-tuning time, and why?
choices: Usually shorter, because fewer parameters are updated
Usually longer, because more iterations were needed to converge
Usually longer, because LoRA adds a second decoder
About the same, because the encoder stays frozen
answer: Usually longer, because more iterations were needed to converge
label: Results · LoRA

stem: In μSAM's few-image COVID IF fine-tuning, how long did training take on CPU versus GPU?
choices: 1.5 h on CPU vs 10 min on GPU
12 h on CPU vs 2 h on GPU
5.3 h on CPU vs 30 min on GPU
30 min on CPU vs 5 min on GPU
answer: 5.3 h on CPU vs 30 min on GPU
label: Results · training time

stem: For fine-tuning on EM neurite segmentation, which starting model do μSAM's authors recommend?
choices: The EM generalist
The LM generalist
A randomly initialised ViT-B
The default SAM model
answer: The default SAM model
label: Results · starting model

stem: How does the μSAM napari plugin perform automatic segmentation of volumetric data?
choices: Per-slice AIS or AMG, merged across slices afterwards
A 3D decoder applied to the whole volume
Orthogonal-slice predictions combined as in CellPose
AIS on a maximum-intensity projection
answer: Per-slice AIS or AMG, merged across slices afterwards
label: Results · volumetric automatic

stem: How does μSAM extend interactive segmentation to volumes and time series?
choices: Interpolates user prompts linearly between annotated slices
Projects masks to adjacent slices or frames and reruns SAM
Runs a separate optical-flow tracker between frames
Feeds the whole stack as video to SAM 2
answer: Projects masks to adjacent slices or frames and reruns SAM
label: Results · interactive 3D/tracking

stem: In μSAM's brightfield organoid user study, why did the LM generalist give worse interactive segmentation than default SAM?
choices: Its masks were too small
It missed organoids at image edges
Its masks were too big
It merged neighbouring organoids
answer: Its masks were too big
label: Results · organoid generalist

stem: In the organoid user study, why were annotation times faster with μSAM's LM generalist than with default SAM?
choices: Its interactive masks were more accurate
It ran on a faster encoder
It needed no embedding precomputation
Its automatic segmentation was better
answer: Its automatic segmentation was better
label: Results · generalist speed

stem: In the organoid user study, how did annotation with pretrained (not fine-tuned) SAM compare with pretrained CellPose?
choices: Slightly faster, but lower quality against consensus
Slightly slower, but higher quality against consensus
Much faster, with equal quality
Slower, and lower quality against consensus
answer: Slightly faster, but lower quality against consensus
label: Results · pretrained SAM vs CellPose

stem: In μSAM's organoid user study, how did tool-assisted annotation compare with fully manual annotation in speed?
choices: Faster only after fine-tuning
Much faster than manual in all cases
Faster only with μSAM, not CellPose
About as fast as manual
answer: Much faster than manual in all cases
label: Results · vs manual

stem: On the separate organoid test split, what happened to μSAM and CellPose after fine-tuning on user annotations?
choices: CellPose improved, μSAM deteriorated
Both improved by similar amounts
μSAM improved, CellPose deteriorated
Both deteriorated slightly
answer: μSAM improved, CellPose deteriorated
label: Results · test generalization

stem: What did μSAM's authors qualitatively observe behind the fine-tuned CellPose models' decline on the organoid test split?
choices: They merged adjacent organoids
They drew outlines too large
They detected debris as organoids
They found fewer organoids
answer: They found fewer organoids
label: Results · CellPose decline

stem: What was μSAM's overall verdict on μSAM versus CellPose for brightfield organoid annotation?
choices: No clear winner: CellPose starts better but generalizes worse
μSAM is better throughout and generalizes better
CellPose is better throughout and generalizes better
No clear winner: μSAM starts better but generalizes worse
answer: No clear winner: CellPose starts better but generalizes worse
label: Results · organoid verdict

stem: In μSAM's volume-EM nucleus user study, why did the default ViT-B model work slightly better than the EM generalist?
choices: Fly larva nuclei are not roundish organelles
Likely resolution differences from the training data
The EM generalist was never trained on nuclei
The data were imaged in high-energy X-ray
answer: Likely resolution differences from the training data
label: Results · 3D study model choice

stem: In μSAM's volume-EM nucleus study, what was the average annotation time per object with ilastik carving versus fine-tuned μSAM?
choices: 84 s vs 24 s
120 s vs 84 s
120 s vs 24 s
24 s vs 84 s
answer: 120 s vs 24 s
label: Results · 3D annotation time

stem: How did μSAM's nucleus-tracking user study make the Schwartz et al. dataset more challenging?
choices: Added synthetic noise to each frame
Downsampled each frame by a factor of three
Removed the first third of each time series
Used only every third frame
answer: Used only every third frame
label: Results · tracking design

stem: In μSAM's nucleus-tracking user study, how did the LM generalist compare with default SAM?
choices: It tracked nuclei clearly better
It tracked nuclei clearly worse
It was faster but tracked worse
It performed about the same
answer: It tracked nuclei clearly better
label: Results · tracking generalist

stem: In μSAM's tracking study, what did fine-tuning the LM generalist on a separate time series change?
choices: It roughly halved tracking time
It did not speed up tracking further
It raised tracking accuracy above TrackMate's by a wide margin
It enabled fully automatic tracking
answer: It did not speed up tracking further
label: Results · tracking fine-tuning

stem: How did μSAM's interactive tracking compare with TrackMate (with StarDist) in the user study?
choices: A bit faster, but lower-quality annotations
Much faster, with similar quality
A bit slower, but higher-quality annotations
Slower, and lower-quality annotations
answer: A bit slower, but higher-quality annotations
label: Results · vs TrackMate

stem: In μSAM's tracking user study, about how long did TrackMate take per track?
label: Results · TrackMate time

stem: Why did μSAM report segmentation accuracy at IoU 50% rather than mean segmentation accuracy in the COVID IF fine-tuning experiment?
choices: Mean segmentation accuracy was too stringent for the small objects
IoU 50% is the COVID IF challenge's official metric
Mean segmentation accuracy cannot score LoRA models
Ground truth existed only as bounding boxes
answer: Mean segmentation accuracy was too stringent for the small objects
label: Results · fine-tuning metric

stem: Why does μSAM not offer CellPose-style human-in-the-loop fine-tuning after each annotated image?
choices: napari plugins cannot run training in the background
Fine-tuning SAM takes too long, especially on the CPU
Updating after each image caused catastrophic forgetting
SAM's licence forbids continual retraining
answer: Fine-tuning SAM takes too long, especially on the CPU
label: Discussion · no HIL

stem: What 3D strategy used by CellPose and MitoNet does μSAM forgo because of its computational cost?
choices: Running per-slice 2D inference
Merging per-slice masks in post-processing
Predicting on orthogonal slices
Precomputing image embeddings
answer: Predicting on orthogonal slices
label: Discussion · 3D limitation

stem: What caveat do μSAM's authors attach to their comparisons against CellPose and MitoNet?
choices: Those tools were run only on the CPU
Those tools were scored on a different test split
Those tools were given interactive corrections
Those tools were not retrained on μSAM's training data
answer: Those tools were not retrained on μSAM's training data
label: Discussion · comparison caveat
